lines.en: I tap on Haruka’s name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
We talked recently about spending some time together at her place and watching movies or something along those lines, so I figure now is as good a time as any to make that dream a reality.
And when I say “dream,” I mean it very loosely as my dreams are much more exciting.
When I actually have them, that is.
Lately, I haven’t been having-
: Hey! What’s up?
: Oh, hey. Nothing really.
: Are you free tonight?
: As a matter of fact, I am. Sara just bailed on me and Molly is “managing” the cafe tonight.
: And you’re sure the cafe is going to be okay?
: Nope! But I really don’t want to think about work right now.
: Come over and let’s do stuff.
: I’d offer to pick you up but I’m feeling really lazy and don’t want to leave right now.
: Wow. Thank you for the kind offer, but I will walk.
: I know you will!
: See you soon!
Haruka hangs up the phone and, before I know it, I’m walking to her place.
The walk to Haruka’s is always kind of annoying.
I should probably invest in a car sooner or later, but...
I don’t know.
I’ve gotten kind of familiar with these streets over my time here.
I’m memorizing them quicker than I’ve memorized anything, I think.
Besides things that are meant to be memorized like phone numbers or addresses.
You know what I’m talking about.
The process of remembering things that you are only kind of supposed to remember.
Like streets or the names of distant relatives.
Like how many beeps the microwave makes after it finishes blasting radiation into a frozen TV dinner.
These are things we memorize subconsciously as opposed to consciously.
But the more time I spend here, the more I move from the former form of memorization to the latter.
I want to memorize these streets.
I feel I’ll be spending a concerning amount of time traversing them if nothing goes horribly wrong in the near future.
I arrive at Haruka’s place after what seems like half an hour and ring the bell.
: Hey! How was your walk?
: Unnecessary.
: Well, on the bright side, you get to see me now. So that’s at least slightly rewarding, right?
: Slightly, yeah.
: Awesome. I’m almost worth a thirty minute walk.
: I’ve gotta say this is personally better than I ever thought I’d do, sooooo hooray for Haruka!
: I’ve only been here for ten seconds and the self-esteem issues are already coming out.
: Tonight is going to be a blast.
: Hey, you knew what you were signing up for and you still came either way.
: I even gave you the chance to say “No, I don’t want to walk all the way over there,” and yet, here you are.
: So, since you’re here, I guess it’s finally time we find something to do, huh?
: What would the gameplan have been if I never came?
: I told you at the cafe, didn’t I? Probably ice cream and crying.
: You can still eat ice cream if you want.
: I’d have to run out and buy some.
: Want me to cry instead?
: Not really. I never know what to do around girls when they cry.
: Uhh, how often are you around crying girls?
: Often enough for this to be an actual thing I have learned about myself.
: Fair enough. What you do on your own time isn’t really my business.
: Know what is my business, though?
: What, Haruka?
: Koi Cafe.
: Get it?
: Cause like-
: Yeah.
: Okay, well it’s been fun. I’ll see you later.
: Oh, come on! That was good!
: Here, come sit down. It’s no fun just standing near the door and listening to me tell jokes.
Well, she’s right about that, at the very least.
Haruka walks over to her sofa, grabbing the TV remote off the table in front of her and turning up the volume on whatever program she was watching before I got here.
I walk back to the entryway and kick my shoes off after I realize I forgot to remove them before taking my place next to her on the couch.
: So, welcome to a day in the life of me.
: When I’m not making cappuccinos or bossing around a bunch of mini versions of myself, I’m doing this.
: Sitting on a couch and contemplating what sort of person I am while watching Gordon Ramsay make children feel bad about themselves on Master Chef Junior.
: You lead an interesting life, Haruka.
: Don’t tease me.
: Even before my husband was drafted, it was like this- just with two bodies on the couch instead of one.
: So you weren’t happy even when he was around?
: I never said that.
: When you love someone, you can do things like just sit on a couch with them and watch Gordon Ramsay yell at children and it will feel like the most fun you’ve had in forever.
: It isn’t until they’re gone that you realize how depressing it is to be watching TV alone.
: This conversation got serious much quicker than I expected it to.
: Hahaha...yeah. Sorry about that. I’ve just...gotten so used to doing things like this with him that I find myself reliving those days any time I turn on Netflix.
: Which sounds kind of shitty to say since he’s still alive-
Maybe.
: But...yeah. Let’s talk about something else. Like...
: Like, what’s it like being a[school] teacher?!
: That sounds like a lot more fun than what I do.
: You’re only saying that because you’re apparently hot for [teenage]girls.
: Yup. You got me.
: Now tell me what it’s like.
Huh.
How I feel about teaching...
: It kind of sucks.
: That...is not the answer I expected.
: Why would you say that?
: With how much I’ve heard about you in[school] from Rin, I always kind of thought you liked your job.
: You know, the whole touching youths thing.
: Just to clarify, which sort of “touching youths” are you referring to right now?
: The not-creepy one this time.
: Aren’t you interested in making differences in these girls lives or something like that?
: How’d you get into teaching in the first place?
: It just...kind of happened.
: So you just kind of happened to go to[school] for years to become a teacher and then just kind of applied for a teaching job?
: No I mean it literally just kind of happened.
: You wouldn’t get it.
: Try me.
: It involves time travel.
: Okay, never mind.
: It’s clear you’re not going to be serious, so we can just move on to something else.
Oh well.
Can’t say I didn’t try.
: You know, I used to have a crush on my [high_school] teacher when I was around Rin’s age.
: Granted, I was too much of a coward to ever tell him that. And it’s not like I would have expected anything to have happened even if I did.
: Worried about the age gap thing?
: More like there just...wasn’t anything notable about me.
: I was just a normal girl living a normal life and studying just like any other normal person until, one day, I met the guy who I would end up marrying.
: And suddenly we’re back at your husband.
: Fuck! Sorry. I didn’t mean to. It just keeps happening.
: It’s fine. If it was that big of a deal, you wouldn’t keep inviting me over.
: Yeah...You’re...probably right about that.
: And besides, we’re just friends so...
: It’s not like I love you or anything like that.
: You’re just...keeping me company.
: That’s all.
Haruka justifies her betrayal of a man who has not yet been confirmed dead in the only rational way she’s able to think up.
She pretends the touch of my hands and the length of my cock are only temporary respites given to a woman in grief despite her unmeasurable levels of uncertainty.
I can see through her.
Anyone could if they’d just open their eyes.
She is horrible- just like me.
We fit each other well.
Physically and non-physically.
She knows it too.
It’s one of the many reasons she continues to cry nearly every time we fuck.
That’s right.
As it stands, all I am to Haruka is a friend.
Could I change that if I truly applied myself?
Probably.
But would it be right to do so?
Who knows?
It’s not really my place to say.
If she thinks betrayal is the path that will make her feel whole, it’s a path she’s likely to take with or without me.
All I can really do for the time being is continue to be near her.
To quell the unending loneliness of a woman unloved.
: Right. We’re just friends.
: Exactly! Which is why it’s cool for us to do stuff like hang out on my couch and just...talk or...whatever it is we’re doing now.
: Right.
: Now, your relationship with Maki on the other hand...
: Ugh. She’s so hot, though!
: And he already signed off on that so it’s totally okay!
: Besides, it really does only happen on rare occasions when we’re drunk.
: And you know firsthand what kind of wonders she can work with her tongue!
: This is very true. That was most definitely not her first time.
: Probably her millionth!
: Okay now that just can’t even be possible.
: Maki’s...a different type of animal compared to someone like me.
: She’s like this crazy sex goddess and I’m some girl who was too scared to even touch herself until senior year of [high_school].
: I get nervous around her and just kind of...follow her lead.
: Were you really that late of a bloomer?
: I’ve only ever been with two guys before...
: That includes kissing, too.
: Well, not counting girls.
: My husband is the only guy I’ve ever been with...
: I’ve never even kissed anyone else.
: Well, not counting girls.
: If it’s any consolation, the amount of girls you kiss makes no difference to me.
: Feel free to shoot for the world record if you want.
: I will support you every step of the way.
: Even when I start coming for all of the girls in your class?
: Start with Rin. I frequently worry that she’ll explode if she doesn’t find an outlet for her pent-up lesbian energy soon.
: How about we share her?
: Deal. Sign me up.
: I’m gonna tell her you said that~
: Fine by me.
: Also, what is the meaning of this?
: I don’t have Rin’s number yet and I feel like I’m much closer to her than you are.
: She works for me, dude. I need her number to send her pictures of the schedule.
: Do you want it?
: I hope you mean her number and not a picture of the schedule.
: What, so you don’t want to come work for me?
: I can’t say I do.
: I’ll accept a phone number, though.
: Fine. Here.
Haruka begins listing the digits of Rin’s phone number and I carefully type them into my phone.
Congratulations! You have received Rin’s phone number in an extremely roundabout way!
You can now call her to hang out on afternoons, but she will likely be confused when she realizes she never personally gave you her number!
: This is a big victory for me.
: Well I’m sorry to be the bearer of bad news but I’ve got a big loss for you coming up next.
: What? What happened?
: So when I told Rin just now that we were talking about sharing her-
: You actually told her that? I thought you were kidding.
: Well, what I really said was, “Would you date your teacher?”
: Why? You completely removed yourself from the equation and this was entirely your idea.
: I’m testing the waters. Just be happy I gave you her number.
: Haruka, what the fuck?
: Well anyway, all she texted back was the upside down smile emoji.
: That could mean anything.
: Mmm...I think in this case it means “I’d rather date you, Haruka. You’re so pretty and your boobs are great.”
: You sound like a grown-up version of my [niece].
: Wanna give me her number in exchange for Rin’s?
: I don’t think she’s your type. And also no.
: Fine. Looks like I’ll just have to send Rin a wink emoji and forever ruin your chances of romancing her.
: I’ve been around these girls long enough to know how they operate and-
: Woah!
: Woah what? What happened?
: Did Rin say something else?
: No, but Molly did.
: You texted her too?
: It was a group text with the two of them.
: You didn’t even do it privately?...
: What did Molly say?
: Six eggplant emojis and then water droplets.
: Is that good? That sounds good.
: Too good. You should be worried.
: Well, at least I went one for two.
: You’re gonna tell me if anything happens, right?
: Probably not.
: And you call yourself my friend...
Haruka and I hang out for a while longer and she continues to lecture me on the meanings of different emojis.
I immediately forget all of them because it is a stupid conversation topic and I honestly just don’t care.
Eventually, I wind up walking home-
And once again thinking about how nice it would be to memorize these streets.
Haruka’s affection has increased to [haruka_love]!
